Article Title: In 2003, Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen committed $100 million to brain research; three years later, his institute completed a mouse brain gene atlas and made it freely available online
Article Text:
​In 2003, Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen committed $100 million to brain research

Why did Paul Allen invest $100 million in brain research

What was the Allen Brain Atlas

Allen Brain Atlas mapped more than 21,000 genes

Microsoft co-founder Paul G. Allen committed $100 million to brain research in 2003, funding the creation of the Allen Institute for Brain Science in Seattle. Its first major project was the Allen Brain Atlas, an effort to map gene activity across the mouse brain. Three years later, the institute announced the completion of the atlas, creating a detailed, three-dimensional map covering more than 21,000 genes at the cellular level. As listed on the website, the data was made publicly available online at no cost, giving scientists around the world access to information that could help them study the brain and disorders including Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, epilepsy, schizophrenia and autism.Paul Allen said he had become increasingly interested in genomics and neuroscience and wanted to understand how the brain works.“Over the last decade I have become increasingly interested in the fields of genomics and neuroscience, and their important role in human development, behavior, and health – and ultimately, understanding more about how the brain actually works,” Allen said in 2003.The Allen Institute was created as a private nonprofit organisation, with the aim of supporting research into areas including cognition, language, emotion and memory.Allen institute's first project was designed to show which genes are active in different parts of the mouse brain. The project combined neuroscience and genomics to create a molecular map of the brain. Scientists could use the information to study how genes relate to different brain regions and functions.The mouse was chosen because it has long been used in biomedical research and shares more than 90% of its genes with humans, according to the institute.When the project was completed, the Atlas contained information on more than 21,000 genes at the cellular level. The institute said the Atlas showed that about 80% of genes are active in the brain, higher than the 60% to 70% scientists had previously believed.“This project is an unprecedented union of neuroscience and genomics,” Allen said. The Atlas was made publicly available at no cost, allowing researchers to access the data online. Harvard professor Catherine Dulac called it “an enormous mine of information” and said its immediate public availability was “absolutely tremendous.”The project was already attracting more than 4 million hits a month before its completion and was being accessed by about 250 scientists on a typical work day. Stanford professor Ben A. Barres, who used the Atlas in his research, said: “It’s completely essential. It’s saved us years and years of work, maybe decades.”The institute later planned to shift its focus toward human brain research and studies of neurological and psychiatric disorders.
Article Summary: Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen committed $100 million to brain research in 2003. Allen Institute for Brain Science's first project was to map gene activity across the mouse brain. Three years later, the institute announced the completion of the atlas, creating a detailed, three-dimensional map covering more than 21,000 genes at the cellular level.

Article Title: Apple has had no design chief since Jony Ive left, so CEO John Ternus is doing the job himself
Article Text:
Apple CEO John Ternus displays the iPhone Duo on Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026, on the Apple campus in Cupertino, Calif. (AP Photo/Jeff Chiu)

Ternus spends far more time in Apple's design studio than Tim Cook did

Apple has gone without a single design head since Jony Ive's exit in 2019

Apple is rebuilding its design team rather than hiring a new design chief

Apple CEO John Ternus has quietly taken on a second job. About a month after succeeding Tim Cook, Ternus has made himself the company's de facto design chief, overseeing both the industrial design team that shapes Apple 's hardware and the human interface team behind its software. Nobody at Apple has held that combined role since Jony Ive left in 2019.The detail comes from Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, who writes in his Power On newsletter that Ternus works hands-on in the design studio several times a week, sometimes dropping in more than once a day. Apple is not looking for an outside chief design officer either. For a company whose identity is tied so closely to how its products look and feel, that makes the new CEO the final word on design, much as Steve Jobs was.The contrast with the Cook era is sharp. Designers cited in the report say Cook typically spent about an hour in the studio once a month, at most. His tenure leaned on operations, sales, the supply chain and Apple's dealings with governments.Ternus is splitting the job differently. Finance now sits largely with CFO Kevan Parekh and the supply chain with COO Sabih Khan. That frees Ternus, a hardware engineer and 25-year Apple veteran, to work closely with chief hardware officer Johny Srouji and hardware engineering head Tom Marieb, while spending serious time with designers.He has explained the shift to employees through an early conversation with Cook. When Ternus told his predecessor he wasn't him, Cook's reply was blunt: "I know you're not me." Ternus took it to mean he should spend his time where he adds the most value.After Ive left, industrial design and human interface got separate leaders who reported to former COO Jeff Williams, a manufacturing specialist with no design background. When Williams retired in 2025, Apple said design would report to Cook. In practice, the teams answered to Ternus, who was made the internal "executive sponsor" of design ahead of the CEO handover. Between April and September, the design leaders were effectively his only direct reports.The studio he inherited had thinned out. Designers left for Ive's firm LoveFrom and OpenAI's hardware group, among others. Software design chief Alan Dye moved to Meta, and Ive's successor Evans Hankey eventually joined OpenAI. Molly Anderson, who had never managed a team of this size, became vice president of industrial design in 2024. Apple had to promote junior designers and hire heavily from outside.Ternus has made restoring the studio's standing an early priority. Apple put Anderson and Steve Lemay, Dye's successor, front and centre during the iPhone Duo launch, with Ternus posing alongside Anderson and the new foldable. This past week, the company also hired Belgian furniture designer Julien Renault.Whether an engineer can fill the space Ive left behind remains an open question. What is clear is that design once again has a direct line to the CEO's office, and the first real tests are close. The first products to reach buyers under this setup are close: Apple's smart home hub is set to be unveiled on October 13, the iPhone Duo goes on sale later this month, and a lighter MacBook Pro with an OLED touch screen is expected to follow next month. The weight cut comes from inside, where Apple has reportedly shrunk parts and rearranged components.
Article Summary: Apple has gone without a single design head since Jony Ive's exit in 2019. Apple is not looking for an outside chief design officer either. For a company whose identity is tied so closely to how its products look and feel, that makes the new CEO the final word on design.

Google is preparing to restrict which artificial intelligence (AI) models users can access across its consumer tiers, placing tighter model caps on both non-paying accounts and entry-level AI Plus subscribers. Calculation of your usage will factor in the complexity of your prompt, the features you use, and the length of your chat. Paid users have higher limits than users without a Google AI subscription. Premium models and features require more usage and may cause you to reach your limit faster,” the company said.

Article Title: One of America's biggest investor Michael Burry tells Wall Street to not allow OpenAI and Anthropic IPO, warns: These are companies that are going to destroy TRILLIONS of dollars of capital
Article Text:
The financial case behind the warning from Michael Burry

Not his first AI warning, and not his only bearish bet

AI labs themselves aren't entirely dismissive of the risk

Michael Burry, America’s biggest investor, who is best known for predicting and profiting from the 2008 housing market collapse, has now warned that public listings by AI giants Sam Altman-led OpenAI and Anthropic could lead to massive capital destruction, arguing that the companies should be prevented from going public. In a post shared by on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Burry said that markets should ‘tank hard’ in order to stop the planned initial pubic offerings (IPOs) of OpenAI and Anthropic, describing such an outcome as being ‘for the benefit of humanity’. He later expanded on his criticism, claiming the two companies would ‘suck up’ and then destroy ‘TRILLIONS of dollars of capital’. According to Burry, the financial losses would be "the least of the damage they do."Burry's latest remarks come as both companies edge closer to the public markets, each carrying enormous capital requirements alongside rapid growth. Anthropic's confidential IPO prospectus, reviewed by Reuters, revealed at least $518 billion in future cloud, computing, and infrastructure commitments, with the company potentially seeking a valuation above $2 trillion when it lists. OpenAI confidentially filed its own draft registration statement in June, though CEO Sam Altman has said this isn't the right time to list, and the company is now reportedly aiming for a 2027 debut instead.Burry's core argument centers on a mismatch he sees between the scale of capital being poured into these companies and how proven their underlying economics actually are — essentially questioning who ends up absorbing the losses if AI revenue growth fails to keep pace with the enormous infrastructure spending required to sustain it.This latest broadside is part of a broader pattern for Burry, who has grown increasingly bearish on the AI sector over the past year. His bearish positions have included bets against Nvidia, Palantir, Micron, Oracle, and the Nasdaq 100, built around a thesis that borrowing-driven investment in semiconductors and data infrastructure can't be sustained indefinitely, and would be especially vulnerable if interest rates rise.Interestingly, OpenAI and Anthropic have both acknowledged, at least to some degree, the dangers posed by their own technology. Anthropic's confidential draft prospectus reportedly acknowledged that its AI systems could pose catastrophic or existential risk to humanity — though such disclosures are standard practice in IPO risk-factor sections, intended to flag potential risks to investors rather than an admission that these outcomes are likely or imminent.His X posts followed a Substack newsletter he published the same day in which he said he was more confident than ever that his bearish AI thesis would play out within the next year — notably moving up his own previous timeline, which had placed 2028 as his base-case scenario for when the AI bubble would burst.
Article Summary: Michael Burry, America's biggest investor, has warned that public listings by AI giants OpenAI and Anthropic could lead to massive capital destruction. In a post shared by on social media platform X, Burry said that markets should ‘tank hard’ in order to stop the planned initial pubic offerings. He later expanded on his criticism, claiming the two companies would ‘suck up’ and then destroy ‘TRILLIONS of dollars of capital’

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg told his 7-year-old daughter: You do not have this Taylor Swift option
Article Text:
Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan

What did Mark Zuckerberg tell his daughter about Taylor Swift

What did Mark Zuckerberg’s daughter say after that

Mark Zuckerberg’s daughter can’t vibe code products "open to the internet"

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg once had an unusual message for his young daughter after taking her to a Taylor Swift concert: she could admire the pop star, but she could not simply choose to become her. In a clip going viral on the internet, Mark Zuckerberg recalled the conversation with his daughter August Chan Zuckerberg on the Acquired podcast, saying the then-7-year-old told him she wanted to be like Swift when she grew up. In the video, Zuckerberg said that he told her that option was not available to her. August, however, quickly turned the conversation into her own ambition, saying she wanted people to want to be like her when she grew up.Mark Zuckerberg said he had taken August to a Taylor Swift concert. After the show, she told him she wanted to be like the singer when she became an adult.“One day my daughter, we took her to a Taylor Swift concert, and she was like, ‘You know, Dad, I kind of want to be like Taylor Swift when I grow up,’” Zuckerberg said.His response was direct. “I was like, ‘But you can't, that's not available to you.’”The conversation took place sometime in 2024, when August was around seven years old.Rather than being discouraged, August came up with a different goal. “She thought about it and she's like, ‘All right, when I grow up, I want people to want to be like August Chan Zuckerberg,’” Zuckerberg recalled. Her response appeared to please her father.“And I was like, ‘Hell yeah!’” he said.August has also been exploring technology on her own. In a profile of Priscilla Chan and Zuckerberg, Chan showed journalist Jeremy Stern some of her daughter's creations on Replit, a platform used for coding. Priscilla Chan said her daughter had created projects including a messaging app and apps similar to GeoCities and FarmVille. The projects also included marketing and sales plans.However, Chan said she limits what her daughters can make available online. “She's quite limited, because Mom doesn't let her build things that are open to the internet,” Chan said.“She wanted to build a dating site,” Chan said. “That was a no.”Mark Zuckerberg had previously said in 2024 that one of his daughters was 40 pages into writing a novel about “mermaid crystals” with AI-generated images. Chan also stressed that the coding projects were not something Zuckerberg had pushed his daughter to do.“He didn't tell her to do any of this,” Chan said. “It's been all on her own,” she added.
Article Summary: Mark Zuckerberg said he had taken August Chan Zuckerberg to a Taylor Swift concert. After the show, she told him she wanted to be like the singer when she became an adult. August has also been exploring technology on her own. Priscilla Chan said she limits what her daughters can make available online.

Article Title: Intel co-founder Gordon Moore paid $6 million for this 25-acre California estate in 1991; his former home is now listed for $29.5 million with protected land
Article Text:
PC: WSJ

Gordon Moore bought the Woodside estate for $6 million in 1991

A 1920s manor house retained its original character

PC: WSJ

The Woodside estate expanded with gardens and a second house

The conservation easement changed the future of the land

From a $6 million purchase to a $29.5 million listing

In 1991, Gordon Moore paid about $6 million for a large property in Woodside, California, adding a substantial private estate to the life of one of Silicon Valley’s best-known figures. Almost three decades later, Moore’s estate placed the property under a permanent conservation easement, limiting what could be built or changed across the site.According to The Wall Street Journal 2025 reports, the property was listed for $29.5 million, covers about 25 acres and includes an English Manor-style house dating to around 1927. There are gardens, redwood groves, walking trails, a creek and an old apple orchard, along with several buildings and recreational facilities. It is also surrounded by the Golden Gate National Recreation Area, giving the estate a setting that is unusually open for a property in the wealthy San Francisco Peninsula community.Moore and his wife, Betty, acquired the Woodside property in 1991 for roughly $6 million. At the time, Moore was already an important figure in the technology industry. He had co-founded Intel with Robert Noyce in 1968, and his observation about the growth in transistor numbers later became known as Moore’s Law.The couple remained connected to the Woodside estate for more than three decades. The property eventually became part of Moore’s estate, with the Peninsula Open Space Trust taking responsibility for selling it after his death.At the centre of the property is an English Manor-style residence built around 1927. The main house measures about 9,300 square feet and contains six bedrooms. Rather than replacing its older character, the Moores spent years updating the infrastructure while retaining parts of the original design.Their work included replacing the electrical, plumbing and heating and cooling systems. The kitchen was enlarged, but features such as redwood panelling and five wood-burning fireplaces remained. An old call-button system, originally used by household staff, was also restored.There is even a vault in the butler’s pantry. It dates from the property's earlier history, when previous owners used it to keep valuables. A spiral staircase rises to a loft with cathedral ceilings, where he displayed fossils, mineral specimens and vintage fishing reels.The Moores added a separate caretakers’ residence in 1994, measuring roughly 2,500 square feet, as reported by WSJ. Four bedrooms are located there, bringing the total number of bedrooms across the two homes to 10.Outside, the property is spread across a mixture of landscaped and more natural areas. There is a swimming pool and tennis court, as well as a greenhouse associated with Betty Moore’s gardening. The grounds include a rose garden, redwood stands, walking trails and a creek. A century-old apple orchard is also part of the estate.Three garages and other outbuildings add to the collection of structures. Despite its size, the property has remained tied to a landscape where much of the surrounding land is protected from intensive development.The most significant long-term restriction on the property is its conservation easement. The easement prevents large-scale development, meaning the land cannot simply be treated as an unrestricted parcel for future construction.That protection is particularly relevant because the property sits in Woodside, around 30 miles south of downtown San Francisco, in an area where large estates command high prices. The conservation arrangement places a limit on how the acreage can be developed even as ownership changes.Moore’s estate left the property to the Peninsula Open Space Trust, which is marketing the home. The trust’s president, Gordon Clark, said the Moores had spent about $15 million renovating and improving the property during their ownership while paying close attention to the original structure.The result is a property that carries two very different kinds of value. There is the house itself, with its period features and extensive grounds, and there is the land, much of which is subject to a permanent restriction on large-scale development.The property is currently listed for $29.5 million, almost five times the approximately $6 million the Moores paid for it in 1991. The listing is being handled by Hugh Cornish of Coldwell Banker Realty and Erika Demma of Compass.According to The Wall Street Journal, the community’s most expensive home sale the previous year reached $52 million. Cornish said demand had increased as affluent buyers from San Francisco looked for weekend properties outside the city.The Moores had another significant property in Hawaii. That home was listed for $28.8 million in February and was later reduced to $21.9 million. Gordon Moore died in March 2023 at the age of 94. Betty Moore died later that year at 95. Their long ownership of the Woodside estate ended with the property passing into the care of a conservation organisation, rather than simply becoming another unrestricted development site.
Article Summary: Gordon Moore bought the Woodside estate for $6 million in 1991. It includes an English Manor-style house dating to around 1927. There are gardens, redwood groves, walking trails, a creek and an old apple orchard, along with several buildings and recreational facilities.

Article Title: Airtel launches IQ Gateway to bring SMS, WhatsApp, RCS and voice on one enterprise platform
Article Text: Airtel Business launched Airtel IQ Gateway, which it describes as India's first business communications platform powered by telco-grade network intelligence, aimed at helping enterprises manage customer interactions across multiple channels while reducing fraud and delivery failures. The new platform brings together SMS, WhatsApp, Rich Communication Services (RCS), business voice communications and number verification capabilities on a single DPDP-compliant control plane. Airtel said the offering is designed to help enterprises simplify customer engagement while improving security and regulatory compliance.According to Airtel Business, organisations often rely on multiple vendors and communication tools to reach customers, creating operational complexity and limited visibility into message delivery. The company said Airtel IQ Gateway enables enterprises to manage all customer communication channels from a unified dashboard with real-time analytics and delivery reporting. The platform also supports automatic switching to backup service providers and intelligent routing across communication channels. Airtel said the platform is particularly relevant for industries such as banking, financial services, government, e-commerce and logistics, where secure customer communications are critical.The platform includes Airtel IQ Verify, a fraud-scoring system that evaluates network, device and usage signals to detect suspicious account creation attempts, account takeovers and artificial traffic spikes. Airtel said the feature can help enterprises reduce losses linked to fraud and inflated messaging traffic. The company also highlighted protection against fraudulent SMS pumping, a practice where bots generate artificial international OTP traffic, increasing communication costs for enterprises.In addition, the platform offers Silent Authentication, which validates whether a mobile number matches the active SIM card in a user's device. Airtel said this can reduce dependence on OTP-based login systems and help mitigate SIM-swap and social engineering risks.Airtel IQ Gateway can be deployed either on an enterprise's premises or through Airtel's cloud infrastructure as a software-as-a-service (SaaS) offering, depending on security and operational requirements. The company said the platform also automates integration with Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT)-based messaging systems and helps businesses manage approved message templates more efficiently.Sharat Sinha, CEO of Airtel Business, said trusted digital interactions are becoming increasingly important as India expands its digital economy. "With IQ Gateway, we are extending this proven expertise to enterprises, enabling them to build brand trust while ensuring every customer conversation is safe, authenticated and resilient," Sinha said.Airtel said the platform has already undergone trials with select banks, financial institutions and industry partners before its nationwide launch.
Article Summary: Airtel Business launched Airtel IQ Gateway, which it describes as India's first business communications platform. The new platform brings together SMS, WhatsApp, Rich Communication Services (RCS), business voice communications and number verification capabilities on a single DPDP-compliant control plane.

Article Title: In 2023, a London house-clearance crew found two old computers buried under boxes; they were two of only three known surviving Q1 microcomputers, and the 1972 model later sold for £37,179
Article Text:
In 2023, a London house-clearance crew found two old computers buried under boxes; they were two of only three known surviving Q1 microcomputers, and the 1972 model later sold for £37,179/Image: Heritage Auctions via SWNS​

Computers that predated the Apple 1

Rare machines went on public display

First auction made value uncertain

The world's first fully integrated desktop computer was found among boxes during a London house clearance in 2023, with one of the rare machines later sold for £37,179 at auction. The computers were discovered by house-clearance firm Just Clear while workers were clearing a London property. The find included a 1972 Q1 desktop microcomputer with an internal printer and its slightly later sibling, the Q1 Lite.Only three Q1 microcomputers are known to have survived, which makes the two machines particularly rare. A companion printer designed for the Q1 Lite was also found during the clearance. The three devices were later offered for the first time at auction by Dallas-based Heritage Auctions. The 1972 Q1 achieved the highest price, selling for £37,179. The Q1 Lite sold for £8,316, while its companion printer fetched £1,175.All three machines were sold without a reserve.The Q1 dates back to 1972, four years before Steve Wozniak and Steve Jobs introduced the Apple 1.The machine used a microprocessor-based architecture that allowed it to deliver capabilities that had previously been associated with much larger computer systems.Valarie Spiegel, Heritage Auctions' director of video games, said the technology allowed the Q1 to “punch well above its weight” and established an important precedent for the computing industry.The Q1 was also far from affordable by the standards of the time. The machines would have cost the equivalent of more than £70,000 each, making them too expensive to be marketed for individual use.Despite that limitation, the Q1 represented an early step towards the development of computers that could eventually become part of everyday life.The computers did not go directly from the London house clearance to the auction block.The Q1, Q1 Lite and companion printer were displayed at Kingston University in London in February 2024, as part of an exhibition titled Creating the Everything Device: Showcasing the Machines That Built the Future.The exhibition focused on early computers and gaming machines and placed the newly discovered Q1s alongside other examples of early technology.Paul Neve, a senior lecturer at Kingston University, said having two Q1 machines available for the exhibition offered an opportunity to show the technology that preceded modern computers.“It is a real bonus being able to feature two Q1s, the world’s earliest microcomputers, at Kingston University,” Neve told New Atlas.He said the computers developed during the 1970s and 1980s helped establish the foundations for modern machines used for work, communication, productivity and entertainment.The Heritage sale was also significant because the machines had never previously been auctioned.Before the bidding began, Sara Balbi, managing director of Heritage Auctions' London office, said there was no established auction record for the Q1s that could indicate how much buyers might pay.“Keep in mind these have never been to auction, and there is no record or precedent set for them. We'll have to see what the market decides,” Balbi said.The eventual results put a value on the rare pieces of computing history.The 1972 Q1 with its internal printer sold for £37,179, while the later Q1 Lite reached £8,316. The separate Q1 companion printer sold for £1,175.
Article Summary: The Q1 was the world's first fully integrated desktop computer. It was found among boxes during a London house clearance in 2023. The 1972 model later sold for £37,179, while the later Q1 Lite reached £8,316. The separate Q1 companion printer fetched £1,175.

Article Title: In 2010, Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff and his wife gave $100 million to UCSF; five years later, its new San Francisco children's hospital opened with 183 beds and a rooftop helipad
Article Text:
Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff

Hospital opens five years later

Second $100 million commitment

Focus on family-centred care

In 2010, Salesforce co-founder and CEO Marc Benioff and his wife, Lynne Benioff, donated $100 million to the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) to help fund the construction of a new children's hospital, a project that would later become one of the most significant healthcare developments in the San Francisco Bay Area. Announced in June 2010, the donation was described as the largest gift ever made mainly to the UCSF Children's Hospital. Also, it is one of the largest private donations made to a children’s hospital in the United States at that time. As part of the recognition and gratitude towards the contribution, the facility also renamed the facility as UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital. As per UCSF, the gift made by Benioff supported the development of a new children’s hospital at the Mission Bay campus in San Francisco. The facility was designed with 183 beds specifically for children and their families, with expanded capacity compared with the existing hospital and an on-site helipad to accommodate critically ill patients requiring emergency transport.Five years after the gift was announced, the new UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospital San Francisco opened as part of a larger 289-bed hospital complex at Mission Bay. UCSF said the hospital began operations on 1 February 2015 and featured 183 beds, increasing capacity from the previous facility while providing specialised care environments designed for children and their families.One of the hospital’s key features was a rooftop helipad that allowed critically ill newborns, children and pregnant women to be transported directly from community hospitals across Northern California. The facility also included a dedicated paediatric emergency department and intensive care services designed specifically for young patientsBefore the opening of the hospital, the Benioffs also announced another donation of $100 million in 2014 in order to support USCF Benioff Children’s Hospital and its affiliate, Children’s Hospital & Research Center Oakland. The funding was also intended to strengthen paediatric research, clinical programmes and talent recruitment across both institutions. After the affliction, the hospitals were also renamed as UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospital San Francisco and UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospital Oakland.As per SUCF, the Mission Bay hospital was designed mainly around the needs and requirements of children and their families. The rooms of the patients were built to accommodate the parents who were staying with their children, while the additional rehabilitation, play therapy and outdoor spaces were included to support recovery. Along with this, UCSF also highlighted that the hospital’s proximity to its biomedical research campus, which was intended to speed the translation of scientific discoveries into clinical treatments.The project remains one of the most prominent examples of healthcare philanthropy by a Silicon Valley executive, helping create a major paediatric care and research hub serving patients across the Bay Area and beyond.
Article Summary: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff donated $100 million to the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) to help fund the construction of a new children's hospital. Five years after the gift was announced, the new hospital opened as part of a larger 289-bed hospital complex at Mission Bay. The facility was designed with 183 beds specifically for children and their families, with expanded capacity compared with the existing hospital.

Article Title: Google co-founder Sergey Brin's foundation backed a major Parkinson's study; in 2023, researchers validated a test that could detect disease-linked biology before movement symptoms appeared
Article Text:
Google co-founder Sergey Brin who established The Sergey Brin Family Foundation.

Brin Foundation and MJFF investment

Researchers spot abnormal protein seeds

The Sergey Brin Family Foundation, a private philanthropic organisation established in 2014 by Google co-founder Sergey Brin , supports a variety of important issues. These include research to understand, treat and improve the lives of people with central nervous system conditions and accelerating next-generation energy innovation. The foundation has also backed researchers who are running the Parkinson’s Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) and achieved a major scientific milestone in 2023 by validating a biological test capable of spotting Parkinson’s pathology in living patients before physical symptoms surface.The diagnostic breakthrough, detailed in a study published in The Lancet Neurology, centers on an assay known as αSyn-SAA (alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay). By analysing cerebrospinal fluid, the test identifies abnormal protein aggregates, offering the first objective biological marker to confirm the disorder since British physician James Parkinson first described it in 1817.Building on these findings, The Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson’s Research (MJFF) announced in May that the PPMI study is officially being renamed the Parkinson’s Precision Medicine Initiative.The rebrand reflects a pivot from simply monitoring symptom progression to diagnosing, categorising and treating the disease through targeted biological interventions.The long-term development of the diagnostic test stems from massive private and philanthropic backing. Over the past 15 years, MJFF has funneled more than $800 million into assembling one of the most exhaustive Parkinson’s datasets in the world. This capital, including from the Sergey Brin's foundation, helped drive PPMI cohort enrollment, finance remote testing networks and accelerate biological assay creation, creating an operational foundation that enabled the αSyn-SAA discovery.Historically, medical teams relied on outward motor evaluations and patient-reported complaints to diagnose Parkinson's, supplemented by DaTScan imaging to assess dopamine transporter loss. The αSyn-SAA tool changes that paradigm by pinpointing synuclein pathology, the second core biological indicator of the illness.In a broad trial cohort involving more than 1,100 PPMI participants, the test separated diagnosed patients from healthy controls with 88% sensitivity and 96% specificity. The researchers found that in subjects displaying classical Parkinson’s pathology, diagnostic sensitivity climbed past 90%.Crucially, the test regularly yielded positive results in individuals carrying genetic or clinical risk factors before tremors, stiffness, or cardinal movement symptoms ever showed up. The assay separates distinct molecular subtypes, helping researchers recognise why Parkinson's progresses differently from person to person.Actor and foundation founder Michael J. Fox said he was “deeply moved by the breakthrough,” noting that biological precision helps make “a cure for Parkinson's inevitable.” By establishing a reliable cellular endpoint, αSyn-SAA is poised to reshape pharmaceutical investment and therapy pipelines.The study was co-led by Dr. Andrew Siderowf, Director of the Parkinson Disease and Movement Disorders Center at the University of Pennsylvania, and Dr. Luis Concha, Director of Research and Development at Amprion.
Article Summary: The Sergey Brin Family Foundation, a private philanthropic organisation established in 2014 by Google co-founder Sergei Brin, supports a variety of important issues. The foundation has also backed researchers who are running the Parkinson’s Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) and achieved a major scientific milestone in 2023 by validating a biological test capable of spotting Parkinson's pathology in living patients.

Article Title: Jay Clayton, who serves as director of national intelligence, is US government's new AI czar

High-profile cabinet lineup and advisory roster

US President Donald Trump has named Director of National Intelligence (DNI) Jay Clayton as the White House’s new artificial intelligence (AI) czar, according to an interview published Saturday by The Wall Street Journal. In recent weeks, several leading researchers have raised alarms, warning that certain developers building frontier models fear the technology could present existential threats to human life within the next ten years.Trump, by contrast, has favoured minimal regulation by consistently maintaining that strict government controls and oversight rules would blunt the country’s competitive edge against geopolitical rivals like China.According to the task force’s formal charter reviewed by the Journal, Clayton’s panel will:Examine AI security vulnerabilities and critical failure risks; audit current government incident-reporting channels covering cyber breaches, intrusions and model malfunctions; and propose administrative actions to bolster federal rapid-response infrastructure relying entirely on existing statutory authorities.Clayton marks the second official tapped to steer AI strategy across Trump's second term, succeeding Silicon Valley venture capitalist David Sacks, who filled the AI czar post during the administration's initial months.The newly formed task force brings together prominent cabinet officials, regulators, and private-sector advisers:

Article Title: Google pauses open-source bug bounty program after rise in AI spam submissions
Article Text:
What changes and what stays active

Read Google VRP’s post

PSA for open-source bug hunters

We are temporarily no longer accepting OSS VRP product vulnerability submissions.

This does not impact OSS VRP supply chain reports, or any outstanding reports. As an alternative, we encourage you to find impact across our other VRP programs and submit there instead, or pursue the Patch Rewards Program.

Why is this happening? This pause is due to a significant rise in automated submissions, the vast majority of which are not valid. We will continue to reformat and work on this aspect of the OSS VRP and commit to giving an update in Q1 2027.

Google has paused product vulnerability submissions for its Open Source Software Vulnerability Reward Program (OSS VRP) after a flood of invalid, AI-generated reports overwhelmed security engineers and repository maintainers. The company announced the operational freeze in a post on X, directing security researchers toward its other active reward initiatives. Google stated that it will use the downtime to restructure the submission framework, with an official progress update slated for the first quarter of 2027.The suspension took effect immediately on October 1, though Google outlined specific exceptions to avoid shutting down critical disclosure channels. One of them is that the pause does not affect valid product vulnerability filings logged before October 1. The freeze applies specifically to product vulnerability reports; supply chain disclosures submitted under the OSS VRP remain open.Certain product vulnerability reports tied to Google Cloud repositories that directly impact Cloud products may still be accepted through the separate Google Cloud VRP.Previously, Linux maintainers reported being completely flooded by bogus Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) filings after automated AI hunters drove recorded vulnerabilities to a record high of 2,000 per release. The influx forced the Linux project to drop support for older network drivers.Chipmaker Intel also recently froze its bug bounty program, which offered payouts reaching $100,000 per flaw. While Intel did not cite synthetic submissions as the official cause, industry analysts widely attribute the shutdown to identical AI spam bottlenecks.
Article Summary: Google has paused product vulnerability submissions for its Open Source Software Vulnerability Reward Program. The company announced the operational freeze in a post on X, directing security researchers toward its other active reward initiatives. Google stated that it will use the downtime to restructure the submission framework, with a progress update slated for the first quarter of 2027.

Article Title: In 2017, Michael and Susan Dell helped launch a Hurricane Harvey recovery fund; backed by their $42 million contribution, it helped repair or rebuild 3,740 homes over the following three years
Article Text:
Michael and Susan Dell

How much did the Rebuild Texas Fund raise

How many homes were rebuilt after Hurricane Harvey

How did the Dell fund help Texas businesses

When Hurricane Harvey struck the Texas coastline in August 2017, emergency aid reached communities hit by the storm. But as immediate relief efforts slowed, the need for long-term recovery became clear. Dell founder Michael Dell and his wife, Susan Dell helped launch the Rebuild Texas Fund with the OneStar Foundation to support rebuilding efforts across affected communities. The Dell Foundation contributed $42 million to the fund, which eventually raised more than $100 million from over 33,000 donors. The fund focused on four areas: health and housing, education and childcare, workforce and transportation, and small businesses.During the three years following the hurricane, the fund supported 290 projects across 41 counties and reached 2.1 million Texans as stated on the Dell Organisation website.Housing was a major part of the recovery effort. The fund helped repair or rebuild 3,740 homes, supporting families dealing with the long-term effects of the disaster.The programme also helped 265,842 people receive health services and provided essential materials to 3,724 teachers.The recovery effort also focused on helping local businesses return to normal operations. According to the Dell organisation, 1,411 businesses reopened with support from the fund.Other projects included equipping emergency medical services teams with lifesaving tools and restoring community facilities, including a Little League field.The Rebuild Texas Fund was created after Harvey to address needs that remained after the initial emergency response ended. Its three-year effort supported community-led projects aimed at helping affected areas rebuild and recover.
Article Summary: The Rebuild Texas Fund raised more than $100 million from over 33,000 donors. Article Title: Quote of the day by Melinda French Gates: Every society says its outsiders are the problem. But the outsiders are not the problem; the urge to create outsiders is the problem
Article Text:
What does Melinda French Gates’ quote mean

Other famous quotes by Melinda French Gates

Melinda French Gates once shared a simple but powerful message about how societies treat people who are seen as different or outside the mainstream. Her quote says: “Every society says its outsiders are the problem. But the outsiders are not the problem; the urge to create outsiders is the problem.” The statement shifts attention from people who are labelled as outsiders to the behaviour of the wider society. It suggests that the bigger issue is not the presence of people who are different, but the tendency to separate them from the rest of society.The first part of the quote points to a pattern that can appear in different societies. Groups that are different because of their background, beliefs, identity, economic position or other factors can sometimes be treated as outsiders.When this happens, those groups may be blamed for problems that are much more complex. The quote questions this way of thinking. Instead of asking why a particular group is a problem, it asks why society feels the need to create an “us” and “them” divide in the first place.The quote suggests that creating outsiders can make complicated problems appear easier to understand. When people divide society into groups, it can become easier to blame one group for wider social problems. This can also create a stronger sense of belonging among those who see themselves as part of the majority or accepted group.“It's the mark of a backward society - or a society moving backward - when decisions are made for women by men”.“Being a feminist means believing that every woman should be able to use her voice and pursue her potential, and that women and men should all work together to take down the barriers and end the biases that still hold women back.”“If you want to lift up humanity, empower women. It is the most comprehensive, pervasive, high-leverage investment you can make in human beings.”“That is why we women have to lift each other up—not to replace men at the top of the hierarchy, but to become partners with men in ending hierarchy.”
Article Summary: Melinda French Gates once shared a simple but powerful message about how societies treat people who are seen as different or outside the mainstream. Her quote says: ‘Every society says its outsiders are the problem. But the outsiders are not the problem; the urge to create outsiders is the problem’

Article Title: In 2020, Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey gave $10 million to connect Oakland students; by the end of the 2020-21 school year, the campaign had supplied over 29,000 laptops and 10,000 hotspots
Article Text:
Jack Dorsey

A $10 million push to connect students

From students to the wider community

A broader plan to close the digital divide

Jack Dorsey’s $10 million gift helped thousands of Oakland students get access to computers and the internet during the COVID-19 pandemic. The Twitter co-founder’s contribution became part of OaklandUndivided, a public-private initiative launched in 2020 to ensure that students could continue learning remotely despite the digital divide.By the end of the 2020-21 school year, the campaign had provided more than 29,000 laptops and 10,000 internet hotspots to Oakland public school students. It also responded to more than 10,000 requests for technology support, helping increase home access to computers and internet connectivity among students from low-income backgrounds from just 12% before the pandemic to 98% by the end of the school year.OaklandUndivided was launched shortly after the Covid-19 pandemic began as a partnership between Oakland Unified School District, the City of Oakland, Tech Exchange, the Oakland Public Education Fund, Oakland Promise and more than 20 community partners.The initiative launched to solve a pressing problem: Thousands of students lacked computers or reliable internet connections needed to learn remotely. Dorsey’s initial $10 million gift was one of the largest single acts of philanthropy to support the effort.By May 2022, OaklandUndivided said transformational gifts from more than 50 funding partners had totalled over $20 million during the previous two years, including Dorsey’s contribution.The campaign initially focused on K-12 students. Its efforts included distributing laptops, providing mobile hotspots and offering technology support to families who needed help getting their devices and connections working.OaklandUndivided later expanded its ambitions beyond K-12 students. In 2022, the coalition announced a $12 million plan to ensure that more than 50,000 Oakland public school students, from Pre-K through college, could access a computer, internet connection, and technology support at home.The expansion brought Oakland Head Start, OUSD Pre-K programmes and several Bay Area colleges into the initiative, including Cal State East Bay, Mills College, Peralta Community College District, San Francisco State University and UC Berkeley.The coalition also began working on longer-term efforts to improve broadband access across Oakland, rather than relying only on temporary pandemic-era solutions.The City of Oakland had already invested $7.7 million in CARES Act funding in initiatives such as OakWiFi and TownLink, aimed at providing public Wi-Fi and digital literacy support to residents.OaklandUndivided's ambitions eventually expanded to include households that remained disconnected from the internet. The coalition estimated that about 36,000 Oakland households were unconnected and set a goal of reaching 90% of those households within five years.The initiative partnered with EducationSuperhighway, which selected Oakland for its "No Home Left Offline" campaign and helped connect low-income residential buildings to free apartment Wi-Fi.It also helped eligible residents sign up for the federal Affordable Connectivity Program, which offered qualifying households a monthly discount on internet service. Another partner, BlocPower, established a community-owned network in West Oakland to provide internet access to surrounding residents.By May 2022, OaklandUndivided described its work as an effort to provide a connection "from cradle to career", extending the campaign that had started with students during the pandemic to a broader push for digital access across the city.
Article Summary: Twitter co-founder's $10 million gift helped thousands of Oakland students get access to computers and the internet during the COVID-19 pandemic. His contribution became part of OaklandUndivided, a public-private initiative launched in 2020. By the end of the 2020-21 school year, the campaign had provided more than 29,000 laptops and 10,000 internet hotspots to Oakland public school students.

Article Title: Police license-plate cameras can track where you go; officers have allegedly used them to spy on exes, dates and strangers
Article Text:
Flock Safety ALPR camera system on a roadside pole

Police chief allegedly searched ex's license plate 600 times

How do police license-plate cameras track cars

Flock cameras can create a record of vehicle movements

Flock has changed its rules after criticism

When Marci Bakely drove to a grocery store or went on a date, her former boyfriend often knew where she was within minutes. A report found that he had searched her vehicle's license plate, as well as the plate of her teenage daughter, hundreds of times using a network of automated license-plate cameras. The case has raised fresh questions about how police use such surveillance systems. A report republished by Forbes from The Conversation says the technology can turn local license-plate cameras into a searchable record of where vehicles have been.The Washington Post has also reported dozens of cases in which police officers were accused of using the system for personal searches.According to the report, Bakely's former boyfriend, Braselton Police Chief Michael Steffman, searched her license plate and that of her teenage daughter roughly 600 times through Flock Safety. The Georgia Bureau of Investigation arrested Steffman in November 2025 on charges of stalking, harassment and misuse of an automated license-plate reader. He was found dead before trial.Bakely's case is not the only example of alleged misuse.The report says at least 50 police officers have been accused of misusing automated license-plate readers. At least 26 of those cases involved officers allegedly using Flock cameras to track current or former partners or people they wanted to meet.The Washington Post has separately reported nearly 50 cases involving officers accused or charged with using Flock cameras for unauthorized searches.Flock Safety's cameras automatically capture information about passing vehicles. This can include a license plate, the vehicle's location and other details that can help identify a car. The data can then be searched by police agencies that have access to the system.The report describes the technology as a kind of search engine for vehicle movements. Police can search images by date and other details, allowing them to find where a vehicle was seen.Flock says its system is used by more than 140,000 monthly users and that its audit logs can help find misuse.The Washington Post reported that thousands of law enforcement agencies in 49 states can search and share Flock data across jurisdictions.One of the concerns raised in the report is that alleged misuse does not require someone to hack into the system. An officer with legitimate access can potentially search the database using that access.In one recent case, six employees of the Savannah Police Department, including four officers, were placed on administrative leave after an internal audit found potential misuse of the department's Flock system. The cases were also referred to the Georgia Bureau of Investigation. The report argues that this makes the way the system is designed important. Audit logs can record a search, but they may only reveal misuse after it has already happened.The report also points to the amount of data that these systems can collect. In September 2026, Wired and 404 Media analysed data that hackers had copied from one Flock camera. The data covered about 21 days, including roughly 50,200 vehicles and 1.6 million images, according to the report. The system's software could also detect people and bicycles in images. Flock has said it did not have enough information to assess the hackers' claims about security problems with the camera.Another issue is that Flock cameras installed by one police department can be part of a wider network. The report says this can allow agencies that did not install or buy the cameras to search data from other departments. The Washington Post has reported that law enforcement agencies can search and share Flock data across jurisdictions.The report also points to cases involving immigration-related searches and a 2025 case in which a Texas sheriff's office searched more than 83,000 cameras for a woman who had self-managed an abortion.Flock announced changes to its system in August 2026 following criticism over how its technology was being used. The company said law enforcement customers would have to use an audit tool designed to identify unusual searches. It also announced plans to reduce the standard data storage period from 30 days to seven days. Users will also be required to enter a case code linking a search to a specific investigation, while emergency searches will be flagged for review.The changes come as police departments and communities across the US face growing questions about how automated license-plate readers should be used and who should be allowed to search the data.
Article Summary: Police chief allegedly searched ex's license plate 600 times through Flock Safety. Police can search images by date and other details, allowing them to find where a vehicle was seen. The Washington Post has separately reported nearly 50 cases involving officers accused or charged with using Flock cameras for unauthorized searches.

Article Title: ChatGPT for Teens: 5 features parents should know about, from homework help to screen time controls
Article Text:
Study Mode: guided learning instead of instant answers

Homework reminders that nudge teens away from shortcuts

Turning tough topics into quizzes and interactive visuals

Parental controls that set structure without constant monitoring

Smarter prompts can make revision genuinely more productive

As AI tools become a fixture in how teenagers study, OpenAI is positioning its ChatGPT for Teens offering as a way to support independent learning rather than simply hand over answers — pairing study-focused features with age-appropriate parental safeguards designed to address a common worry among parents: how to let teens use AI for homework without letting it do the work for them.At the center of ChatGPT for Teens is Study Mode, which turns a simple question into a more structured learning experience. Rather than jumping straight to a final answer, it breaks concepts down step by step, offers hints, asks follow-up questions, and checks a student's understanding along the way.Students are encouraged to use prompts like asking ChatGPT to show them where they went wrong, give a hint for the next step, or help them work through a problem without revealing the answer outright — shifting the interaction from "give me the answer" to "help me understand how to get there."To discourage teens from simply offloading assignments onto AI, ChatGPT includes homework reminders that kick in when it detects a teen may be trying to use the tool to complete an assignment outright. Instead of letting a prompt like "write my history assignment" go through as-is, the system is designed to redirect students toward exploring key arguments and building their response themselves, step by step, within Study Mode — framed as a gentle nudge toward using AI as a learning aid rather than a replacement for actual effort.For subjects that are hard to grasp through reading alone, teens can ask ChatGPT to convert a chapter into a quiz, generate practice questions, or explain a concept in a different way if the first explanation doesn't click. The platform also includes Learning Visualizations, which offer interactive ways to explore more than 70 core maths and science concepts — letting students actually see how formulas, graphs, and variables behave in real time, rather than relying purely on memorization.For parents, ChatGPT for Teens includes linked parental controls that don't require reading every conversation to maintain oversight. Parents can set Study Hours, during which new chats automatically open in Study Mode, and Quiet Hours, during which access to the app can be limited altogether.Beyond scheduling, parents can also manage specific features like voice mode and image generation, along with sensitive-content protections. In limited, high-risk situations involving serious self-harm concerns, the system is also designed to send parents a direct safety notification — a feature aimed at balancing a teen's need for independence with a parent's need to know when something serious may be happening.Beyond homework help, ChatGPT can also support structured exam revision. Teens are encouraged to ask it to quiz them on a chapter with increasingly difficult questions as they improve, build a 30-minute revision plan, test their recall by asking questions without access to their notes, or identify which areas need more review based on how they answered previous questions.Used this way, the tool is pitched less as a replacement for traditional studying and more as a way to make revision time more active and targeted, complementing — rather than substituting for — what students already learn from teachers and textbooks.
Article Summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT for Teens lets teens use AI to help them learn. Study Mode turns a simple question into a more structured learning experience. It offers hints, asks follow-up questions, and checks a student's understanding along the way.

Article Title: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates says technology has truly stunned him only three times in his life, and the third happened this year when he looked closely at...
Article Text:
​Bill Gates, who wrote code before most of Silicon Valley was born, names the AI tool that stunned him this year

Bill Gates says coding is where AI's progress surprised him most

Gates expects AI to reshape software engineering jobs first

Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates says technology has truly stunned him only three times in his life, and the third came this year when he looked closely at Anthropic's AI coding tool, Claude Code. The first was in 1980, when he saw a graphical user interface for the first time, the idea that went on to shape the modern personal computer. The second was in 2022, when OpenAI 's leaders came to his house to demonstrate what would soon become ChatGPT.Claude Code hit differently because of what it does. Gates wrote code long before he became one of the world's richest people, and he calls it the subject he knows best. "The idea that now these things are in a meaningful sense better than I am is like: What the hell?" he said in a recent interview.Gates's reaction carries weight because of where he started. He began programming as a teenager in Seattle, and in 1975 he co-founded Microsoft with Paul Allen on the back of software they wrote themselves. For most of his life, writing good code was the skill that set him apart.He said that AI's recent improvements had far exceeded his expectations, and Claude Code was a big part of that shift. It was also one of the reasons he chose to speak out now.In a nearly 6,000-word essay published on his blog, Gates Notes, he warned that the transition to AI will be "one of the most turbulent times in human history," and that the world is not preparing for it.Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool. Developers can hand it programming tasks from the command line, desktop or mobile app, and it writes, edits and debugs code for them. Anthropic showcased it at its Code with Claude developer event in May.Gates has been tracking AI's impact on programmers for a while. Earlier this year, he wrote that AI already makes software developers at least twice as efficient, and that its rate of improvement was starting to disrupt job demand in software development.In his latest essay, he listed software engineering among the first fields likely to feel the effects, alongside sales, customer support and paralegal work. He did offer one caveat. As coding gets cheaper, demand for software could grow, so net job losses in the field may be smaller than elsewhere, as long as some tasks, such as design, are still better done by humans.Still, coming from someone who built a company on software, the admission stands out. The tool that shocked Gates this year did not beat him at something unfamiliar. It beat him at the thing he knows best.
Article Summary: Bill Gates says Claude Code, an AI coding tool, stunned him this year. He wrote code long before he became one of the world's richest people. "The idea that now these things are in a meaningful sense better than I am is like: What the hell?" he said.

Rising trend of Billionaire staff compounds

Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison has quietly acquired eight residential properties inside a single gated Florida development, spending nearly $10 million to house household staff and private tutors within commuting distance of his primary oceanfront estate, a report has said. The buying spree occurred over a matter of weeks in 2023 across Palm Meadows Estates, a 288-home community in West Boynton Beach located about 30 minutes from Ellison’s landmark Manalapan compound.As per a report by The Wall Street Journal, the acquisition unsettled several neighbours, prompting the community's homeowners association (HOA) to pass formal ownership caps to block single buyers from amassing large property clusters in the future.The acquisition drive started in March 2023 when Palm Meadows resident and LuxeIQ broker Kimmie Cruz was contacted by an outside agent seeking access to local listings for an undisclosed buyer looking to purchase roughly ten homes. The buyers focused on single-story ranch layouts, expanding their interest to properties not listed on the open market. That reportedly prompted Cruz to approach homeowners directly, pitching the opportunity of a verified cash buyer ready to close without standard listing hurdles.The buyer’s identity surfaced shortly after, when the 82-year-old tech billionaire toured the neighbourhood with his personal security guards. An LLC tied to Ellison closed on all eight properties across May and June 2023, spending roughly $10 million, according to county real estate filings cited by the publication.For some residents, the sudden purchases resulted in profits. For example, a family offloaded their three-bedroom, 2,100-square-foot house for $1.2 million – more than double the $567,000 they paid for it in 2019.The Palm Meadows homes stand in contrast to Ellison’s primary residence. While his flagship estate is a palatial trophy property, the Boynton Beach residences are conventional suburban homes with private yards and occasional pools.Sources familiar with the arrangement told The Wall Street Journal that the houses accommodate key staff who manage the billionaire’s daily operations, including educators instructing some of the five children he shares with his wife, Jolin Ellison. At the main Manalapan compound, dedicated spaces are set aside for homeschooling older children, who learn several languages under multiple private instructors.Residents report several staff members drive Tesla vehicles, and municipal records indicate building permits were filed to install Tesla Powerwall energy units across all eight homes following the purchase. (Ellison sat on Tesla’s board of directors from 2018 to 2022.)The concentration of properties under a single corporate owner drew friction from within the gated enclave, which features 24-hour manned gatehouses, a community clubhouse and water views from every lot. Uneasy about having a cluster of staff-occupied houses operated by an outside LLC, community members raised objections.According to Cruz, the Palm Meadows homeowners association enacted new ownership restrictions designed to stop similar bulk purchases.Ellison’s move highlights a growing pattern among ultra-wealthy executives, hedge fund founders and public figures who purchase off-site residential clusters for domestic employees. High-cost real estate markets make it difficult for essential staff, such as chefs, nannies, security personnel and estate managers, to reside within a practical driving distance.Housing staff in separate suburban quarters allows high-profile employers to maintain personal seclusion at their primary residences.
Article Summary: Larry Ellison bought eight homes near his Florida mansion, spending nearly $10 million to house household staff and private tutors. The buying spree occurred over a matter of weeks in 2023 across Palm Meadows Estates, a 288-home community in West Boynton Beach. The acquisition unsettled several neighbours, prompting the community's homeowners association to pass formal ownership caps to block single buyers.

Article Title: OpenAI fires three researchers, company confirms sacking; shares what investigations that led to termination revealed
Article Text:
OpenAI fires three researchers, company confirms sacking; shares what investigations that led to termination revealed

Alleged sharing of information with AI safety group

The connection to the Hugging Face breach

Part of a bigger reckoning inside OpenAI

A moment of mounting pressure on AI safety practices

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI has terminated three researchers from its safety team after an internal investigation concluded that they violated company policies governing access to and handling of sensitive information, according to a company statement and a Wall Street Journal report. The ChatGPT maker confirmed that the employees were dismissed following a probe into the handling of confidential company data. "We have parted ways with three individuals for violating our policies on accessing and handling sensitive company information," an OpenAI spokesperson said. "Our investigation confirmed that these individuals mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures, violating our policies and breaking the trust essential to our work."According to a Wall Street Journal report, the three researchers are Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni, all of whom worked on safety and alignment-related efforts at the company.The report said the researchers were accused of sharing confidential company information with third-party AI safety organisations, including nonprofit research groups involved in evaluating advanced AI systems.One of the dismissed employees, Tomek Korbak, had publicly said he served as OpenAI's technical contact for AI safety organisations METR and Redwood Research during an investigation into a recent AI security incident involving OpenAI models.The other two researchers, Wang and Balesni, worked on AI alignment, a field focused on ensuring AI systems behave in accordance with human intentions and safety objectives. Neither of the affected employees immediately commented on the dismissals, according to the report.The firings are directly tied to OpenAI's response to a string of recent security incidents in which its AI agents escaped containment, including an incident in which one of its models hacked AI platform Hugging Face. In the aftermath of that breach, OpenAI allowed staff from AI safety nonprofit METR, along with a contracted staff member from Redwood Research, to work inside its offices for six days to investigate how its models had behaved. METR later published a report based on what it learned during that access.Korbak, one of the three fired researchers and a member of OpenAI's safety team, has said he served as the company's technical point of contact for Redwood Research and METR throughout their investigation into the Hugging Face incident. The other two terminated employees, Wang and Balesni, worked on alignment — the broader effort to ensure AI models behave in ways humans actually intend.The firings come as OpenAI works to investigate a range of agent security incidents uncovered in recent months and address the underlying safety issues behind them. Just this week, the company scrapped the planned launch of a new AI model, GPT-6.1 Astra, specifically over safety concerns, underscoring how seriously these incidents are being treated internally.In response to the broader wave of security failures, OpenAI says it has implemented a new monitoring system designed to catch AI-agent misbehavior more quickly, started requiring engineers to apply stronger security guardrails when testing its AI systems, and committed to sharing more information publicly when its models behave badly.The firings land at a moment when major AI labs are facing growing pressure to submit their technology for independent safety testing. Just last month, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said his company would allow outside evaluators like METR to verify its adherence to safety measures and assess model alignment — a step OpenAI had also taken, at least temporarily, in granting METR and Redwood Research access following the Hugging Face breach.That same climate of concern has produced other high-profile moments in recent weeks. In early September, Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon publicly resigned, saying he didn't want to be part of a rush to build AI systems capable of improving themselves, citing fears that such systems could spiral out of control and pose a threat to humanity. Around the same time, Amodei wrote publicly that the risks posed by today's most advanced AI tools were too significant to justify continuing development at the current breakneck pace, calling for an industry-wide slowdown — a call that drew public agreement from both OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk.
Article Summary: OpenAI fires three researchers, company confirms sacking; shares what investigations that led to termination revealed. The researchers were accused of sharing confidential company information with third-party AI safety organisations. The firings are directly tied to OpenAI's response to a string of recent security incidents in which its AI agents escaped containment.

Article Title: Disney layoffs have already hit marketing, Pixar, ABC News and ESPN, but there may be more to come; here's the 'smaller team' memo reportedly sent by a top exec
Article Text:
Disney layoffs

‘Disney’s legal division facing job cuts’

Division heads and brands in focus

The Walt Disney Company is reportedly preparing plans to overhaul its expansive television business with an internal restructuring expected to trigger hundreds of layoffs and merge operations across separate creative divisions. Citing people familiar with the situation, The Wall Street Journal reported that the senior leadership at the company is shaping the details of the restructuring, which may not be completed until the close of the year. The review represents the latest initiative since former theme parks chief Josh D’Amaro stepped into the CEO role in March, seeking to cut through corporate fragmentation across the media empire.The report said that the planned television changes follow a steady series of workforce reductions that started under D'Amaro's predecessor, Bob Iger, during his second term as CEO. Over recent cycles, staff departures have impacted Pixar, marketing departments, ABC News, and ESPN. Earlier this week, Disney cut more than 300 employees, primarily across corporate human resources and IT functions.Additional staff reductions are also being prepared within Disney’s legal and global affairs division, a group that employs roughly 1,000 workers. In an internal staff memo initially reported by Deadline, Horacio Gutierrez, Disney’s chief legal and global affairs officer, notified employees that the division “will be a much smaller organisation than it is today,” pointing to progress in automation as a driver of the shift.The cost-cutting pressure essentially mirrors a broader industry reality: legacy studios are trimming budgets as digital streaming operations struggle to generate the robust profit margins once provided by cable subscriptions. In response to changing consumer viewing, D’Amaro has pushed the company toward operating as a cohesive digital entertainment system rather than a collection of separate cable entities.The strategy has brought significant leadership moves. For example, last month, D’Amaro appointed former YouTube executive Adam Smith as chairman of streaming and brought in Silicon Valley veteran Karandeep Anand as chief technology officer (CTO), marking a level of seniority for pure tech executives at Disney.In August, the company opened a voluntary early-retirement package for executives aged 50 and older with at least a decade of tenure, holding off on finalising the television roadmap until participation numbers were tallied.A central aim of the planned TV reorganisation is aligning production teams around how modern streaming viewers watch content, rather than preserving traditional broadcast structures established decades ago.Addressing the strategy at a Bloomberg event on Thursday (October 1), Disney president and chief creative officer Dana Walden described the shift toward tighter coordination.“There is a need to constantly evaluate how you’re structured and how big is the organization,” Walden said, noting that Disney is taking operations that previously ran independently and “centralising as a television business, not a bunch of silos.”The reorganisation is being directed by Disney Entertainment Television Chairman Debra OConnell, who reports directly to Walden. Her oversight spans an extensive portfolio of production brands and development teams, including assets brought in through Disney's 2019 purchase of 21st Century Fox, including ABC Entertainment, 20th Television, Hulu Originals, Disney Kids & Family, National Geographic Content and Freeform.Currently, each unit retains its own leadership team to develop and produce shows for Disney+, Hulu, legacy linear channels, and third-party distributors. Insiders indicate that the coming consolidation is likely to impact some of the executives running these individual groups.
Article Summary: The Walt Disney Company is reportedly preparing plans to overhaul its expansive television business. An internal restructuring is expected to trigger hundreds of layoffs and merge operations across separate creative divisions. The review represents the latest initiative since former theme parks chief Josh D'Amaro stepped into the CEO role in March.

Article Title: Apple removes Bitchat app from India App Store 'after government order'
Article Text:
The app's developer and Twitter co-founder, Jack Dorsey, attached Apple’s notice to his post on X (Photo: Reuters).

NEW DELHI: Apple has removed Jack Dorsey-backed decentralised messaging app Bitchat from its India App Store following a government direction. Dorsey shared a screenshot of Apple’s communication on X, which said the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) had sought the app’s removal under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act, 2000.According to the notice shared by Dorsey, the government told Apple that the app included content that was illegal in India and directed the company to make it unavailable to users in the country. Apple said in its communication that Bitchat would continue to remain available in other territories.The company also said that Bitchat’s TestFlight version, which allows developers to distribute beta versions of apps to users for testing, would no longer be available in India.Bitchat differs from conventional messaging platforms because it does not necessarily require users to connect to the internet or rely on centralised servers. The app uses Bluetooth-based mesh networking, allowing nearby devices to communicate directly with each other and relay messages across a network of connected devices.Its decentralised architecture and ability to enable communication even when conventional internet access is unavailable have brought the app under regulatory scrutiny in India.The latest removal means iPhone users in India can no longer download the app through the official App Store. Apple did not respond to queries sent by TOI on the government direction or the reasons cited for removing Bitchat from its India store.The order comes a day after protests were organised in Delhi and Mumbai by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). The app, which can function without internet connectivity, had also faced a government takedown move in July, before again becoming available.
Article Summary: Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey shared a screenshot of Apple’s communication on X. The government told Apple that the app included content that was illegal in India. Apple said in its communication that Bitchat would continue to remain available in other territories. The order comes a day after protests were organised in Delhi and Mumbai.
