Article Title: US FAA clears Boeing 737 MAX software issue, removes hurdle for MAX 10
Article Text:
WestJet first found the software issue

Boeing working on another software update

The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has cleared a software issue affecting some Boeing 737 MAX flight computers, saying it does not pose a safety concern, reports Reuters. The decision removes a major hurdle for certification of the 737 MAX 10, Boeing's largest MAX variant, which has faced delays for years. The FAA said an expert panel found that pilots would retain full control of the aircraft if the issue occurred and would receive clear warnings. The software problem could prevent pilots from using automated flight guidance during a specific landing situation. The FAA had delayed MAX 10 certification earlier this week while it reviewed the issue.As per the Reuters report, the FAA's Corrective Action Review Board met in Seattle on October 1 to examine the software issue. The regulator said the panel's decision was based on the fact that “pilots retain full ⁠control of the aircraft and the indications to the flight crew are clear and unambiguous.”The FAA said the software issue could prevent pilots from accessing automated flight guidance during an unusual landing situation.It could also increase pilot workload during a go-around, when a pilot stops a landing and climbs again to make another landing attempt.Canadian airline WestJet discovered the problem during an entry-into-service test flight nearly two years ago. The airline said the plane's vertical navigation mode, which helps automate the aircraft's vertical flight path, switched off during an approach.WestJet uses the affected U14.1 software on its MAX aircraft and is expected to receive the MAX 10 early next year.“WestJet has received no reports of this condition occurring during normal line operations,” the airline said in a staff memo seen by Reuters. “Very few occurrences have been reported by other operators using U14 or U14.1 because the condition requires a specific sequence of events.”Boeing said it will continue to follow the FAA's lead while its engineers work on the next software update. The company is also working with airlines on a procedure that would allow pilots “to re-enable automated vertical navigation should this situation occur.”The FAA said it will issue a Special Airworthiness Information Bulletin to US airlines and foreign aviation regulators to make them aware of Boeing's guidance.As per the report, the FAA's decision could allow the Boeing 737 MAX 10 to be certified later this month, in line with earlier expectations.
Article Summary: FAA has cleared a software issue affecting some Boeing 737 MAX flight computers. The decision removes a major hurdle for certification of the 737 MAX 10, Boeing's largest MAX variant. The FAA said an expert panel found that pilots would retain full control of the aircraft if the issue occurred.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Michael Dell: If you don't want to make mistakes, I doubt you will be super successful because failure is the best teacher
Article Text:
Quote of the day

“If you don't want to make mistakes, I doubt you will be super successful because failure is the best teacher. Also very important to learn from mistakes and not repeat them!” Michael Dell

What the quote actually means

What went wrong:

Why did it happen:

What could have been done differently:

What information was missing:

What can be changed next time:

How can the same mistake be avoided:

What did the failure teach us:

Why this mindset is more important than it seems

Mistakes are made by everyone. They can happen when you’re learning something new, making decisions at work or pursuing a bigger goal. Mistakes are often viewed as failures, but they can also be lessons failure simply cannot be. We’ve got to find out what went wrong and learn from that.That's the idea behind a quote by Michael Dell, the founder and CEO of Dell Technologies, who said: “If you don't want to make mistakes, I doubt you will be super successful because failure is the best teacher. Also very important to learn from mistakes and not repeat them!” The thought highlights how mistakes and failures can become valuable learning experiences when people take the time to understand them and avoid repeating the same errors.Dell's statement is closely connected to the idea that mistakes are part of learning. Trying to avoid every possible mistake can mean avoiding situations with uncertainty, experimentation, or opportunities to learn something new.Failure can provide information about what did not work. It can reveal weaknesses in an idea, process, or decision and give people a chance to make changes before trying again.But the quote is not simply about accepting failure. What matters more is what happens after a mistake.If the same mistake repeats without understanding what caused it, the experience provides little value.For example, if a business launches a product that fails to attract customers, simply accepting that the product didn't work isn't enough. The company can look at who the product was designed for, what customers expected, how it was marketed, what competitors offered and where the product fell short.Some questions that can help you learn from mistakes include:Identifying the specific problem can make it easier to understand what needs to change.Looking beyond the immediate mistake can help you identify the underlying reason.Considering alternative approaches can provide useful lessons for future decisions.A mistake may happen because you overlooked an important piece of information or it wasn't available at the time.Turning a lesson into a specific change can make it more useful than simply acknowledging the mistake.Creating a new process, checklist or approach can help prevent the problem from happening again.Not every failed attempt produces the same lesson, so identifying the broader takeaway can help apply the experience elsewhere.It is easy to see mistakes as something to be avoided. But a fear of making mistakes can also make people less willing to experiment, take calculated risks or try unfamiliar approaches.That is where Dell's idea becomes important. A mistake does not automatically lead to success, but it can provide information you can use to improve. The value of failure depends largely on whether people examine what happened and apply what they learned.The same approach can apply to everyday challenges. At work, for example, a project may miss a deadline or fail to deliver the expected results. Treating the outcome only as a failure may not help the team improve. Looking at what caused the delay, which assumptions were wrong, and what could change in the next project can turn the experience into a useful lesson.The idea also changes how we view success. Success doesn’t have to be a straight line with no bumps. It’s about trying things out, learning from what you try, and making adjustments along the way.Dell's quote therefore isn't saying failure should be pursued for its own sake. It is that mistakes can become valuable when people learn from them. Understanding what went wrong, making changes and avoiding the same error can turn a setback into an opportunity to improve.
Article Summary: Michael Dell said: “If you don't want to make mistakes, I doubt you will be super successful because failure is the best teacher. Also very important to learn from mistakes and not repeat them!” A mistake does not automatically lead to success, but it can provide information you can use to improve.

Article Title: Vi Business partners with Cisco to expand Hybrid SD-WAN offerings for enterprises
Article Text:
Focus on cloud, security and network management

Vi Business, the enterprise arm of Vodafone Idea, has partnered with Cisco to strengthen its Hybrid SD-WAN portfolio as enterprises increasingly seek secure and scalable networking solutions to support cloud adoption, distributed operations and AI-driven workloads.The collaboration combines Cisco Meraki's cloud-managed networking and secure multi-WAN capabilities with Vi Business' managed connectivity services, aiming to help enterprises modernise their network infrastructure through hybrid networking, integrated security and multi-cloud connectivity.According to the company, the partnership comes at a time when enterprise demand for software-defined wide area networking (SD-WAN) is rising rapidly. Industry estimates project India's SD-WAN market to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 20.5% to reach $14.6 billion by 2031.Vi Business launched its Hybrid SD-WAN solution in 2023 to help enterprises transform traditional wide area networks by combining SD-WAN technology, security capabilities and multi-cloud integration through a managed services model.Under the partnership, the solution will be powered by Cisco Meraki, enabling enterprises to manage their networks through a single dashboard with application-aware routing, performance monitoring, built-in security, Wi-Fi and cellular connectivity features.The telecom operator said customers will benefit from a fully managed service that includes nationwide connectivity, proactive monitoring, lifecycle management and a single point of contact for support and operations. The offering is being delivered through a service-based model, which allows enterprises to avoid upfront capital expenditure while scaling network infrastructure as business requirements evolve.Commenting on the partnership, M P Sunil Kumar, Chief Enterprise Business Officer at Vodafone Idea, said enterprises are increasingly looking for networking solutions that align with evolving business objectives. "By integrating advanced cloud-managed SD-WAN, wired and wireless networking and built-in security, we enable enterprises to centrally manage distributed networks while radically simplifying operations," Kumar said.He added that the combination of nationwide connectivity, managed services and end-to-end support would help organisations build resilient and scalable networks.Ashok Shivashankar, Managing Director, Partner Organization, Cisco India & South Asia, said enterprise networks must increasingly be designed for agility, scalability and security in an AI-first environment."Together with Vi Business, we are helping enterprises modernise their networks with a managed Hybrid SD-WAN solution that enables greater agility, scalability and operational efficiency while accelerating digital transformation," Shivashankar said.The partnership strengthens Vi Business' push into enterprise digital transformation services as organisations continue to invest in cloud infrastructure, remote operations and AI-enabled business applications.
Article Summary: Vi Business, the enterprise arm of Vodafone Idea, has partnered with Cisco. The collaboration combines Cisco Meraki's cloud-managed networking and secure multi- WAN capabilities with Vi Business' managed connectivity services. Vi Business launched its Hybrid SD-Wan solution in 2023 to help enterprises transform traditional wide area networks.

Article Title: TRAI in October 2026 notification to Airtel, Reliance Jio and Vodafone-Idea: Clearly display these prepaid packs and special tariff vouchers; gives deadline
Article Text:
Representative Image

What TRAI order says

TRAI order on STVs

"Provided also that the service provider shall offer Special Tariff Vouchers (STVs) with appropriate reduction in tariff, exclusively for Voice and SMS for:

(i) validities corresponding to each validity period of thirty days and less than thirty days for STV being offered for Voice, SMS and data, whether with or without value added services and;

(ii) validity renewable on the same date of every month and if the date of such renewal is not available in a month, the date of renewal shall be the last date of that month and;

(iii) at least one STV with validity more than (i) and (ii) above, corresponding to the validity period of STVs being offered for Voice, SMS and data, whether with or without value added services. "

Deadline for compliance

India's Telecom regulator TRAI does not seem to be happy with the way the country's mobile service providers -- Reliance Jio, Airtel and Vodafone-Idea -- show prepaid packs and special tariff vouchers. In a notification issued recently, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has asked mobile service providers to prominently display mandatory recharge plans and special tariff vouchers on their websites, mobile apps and exclusive points of sale. These regulations are called the Telecom Consumers Protection (Thirteenth Amendment) Regulations, 2026.TRAI maintains that it has come with new guidelines after receiving complaints from consumers. It further claims that the regulator too has verified that the telecom operators had placed plans on their websites and apps in a manner that they were not easily visible. In a similar notification, earlier this year, TRAI had also mandated telecom operators to issue special tariff vouchers for voice calls and SMS at a lower cost, as they will not come bundled with data services. Under the mandate, telecom operators will have to issue Special Tariff Vouchers (STVs) for voice calls and SMS only, similar to the existing ones that come bundled with data, voice calls and SMS, carrying validity of 30 days or less.For those unaware, an STV works like a booster recharge for prepaid mobile customers, allowing them to avail of extra benefits by paying an additional amount through these vouchers, like making international calls at lower rates, adding the benefit of unlimited calls in the existing plan, among others.While some STVs offering data services are available for a validity of up to 365 days, TRAI's new regulation focuses on vouchers with a validity of 30 days and less. These rules are aimed to help people in rural areas and customers with low paying capacity. Trai has mandated that every telecom operator must offer at least one plan voucher, one Special Tariff Voucher and one combo voucher having a validity of thirty days."...the Authority...hereby directs all telecom service providers to...provide a separate and clearly visible tab or section titled "TRAI-Mandated Packs" containing different types of TRAI mandated vouchers, which shall be visible as the first tab on the prepaid recharge section on the websites and mobile apps of the service providers and shall also be prominently displayed on their other exclusive points of sale," the TRAI order says.The regulator, however, came across complaints from various subscribers to the different types of Trai-mandated vouchers on the websites and to the different types of Trai-mandated vouchers on the websites and mobile applications of the service provider."In some cases, these vouchers are placed under different categories or require consumers to navigate through multiple pages or screens to find them, as a result of which consumers are facing difficulty in locating and subscribing to the vouchers suitable to their requirementsẠạ the regulator said.Similar to Prepaid packs, TRAI acknowledged that upon examination of the websites and mobile applications of various telecom service providers, it was observed that Trai-mandated vouchers are neither displayed prominently nor are easily accessible.Telecom regulator has now directed Reliance Jio, Airtel and Vodafone-Idea to comply with the order within thirty days from the date of issuing the direction (October 1).
Article Summary: Telecom regulator has now directed Reliance Jio, Airtel and Vodafone-Idea to comply with the order within thirty days from issuing it. Trai has mandated that every telecom operator must offer at least one plan voucher, one Special Tariff Voucher and one combo voucher having a validity of thirty days.

Article Title: Google ex-CEO Eric Schmidt: Best programmers don't write code anymore, they...
Article Text:
Eric Schmidt's idea of a top programmer goes to bed at 7 PM

The best programmers won't be replaced by AI—they'll become even more valuable

Schmidt says AI's real impact will be automating the 'boring' backbone of business

Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says the most valuable programmers in the world have quietly redefined their job. They don't write code anymore. They write specifications, set evaluation criteria, hit run—and go to bed. It's a shift that Schmidt believes signals something much larger than a change in workflow—it's the beginning of AI reshaping how entire industries operate.Schmidt described a programmer at one of his startups who does exactly this. Every evening at 7 PM, he defines what he wants the AI to build, writes a test function to judge the output, and lets the system loose. Then he has dinner with his wife and goes to sleep. The AI churns through the night, finishing around 4 AM. By breakfast, the work is done. "This stuff would've taken me six months and 10 programmers at Google," Schmidt said. "This poor guy's sleeping."The natural assumption is that AI will make programmers obsolete. Schmidt thinks the opposite is true—at least for the elite ones. Top-tier engineers were always disproportionately valuable, worth roughly 10 times more than those just below them. That gap, he argued, is about to widen.The grunt work is disappearing, but the ability to orchestrate AI systems at scale—grasping parallelisation, defining the right constraints, judging when the output is good enough—is becoming the entire job.The real skill now isn't writing code, Schmidt suggested. It's framing the problem correctly and knowing what "good" looks like. "If you can define the evaluation function and you can let it run, and if you have enough hardware, you're inventing worlds," he said. AI systems at leading research labs are already handling a significant and growing share of programming work, making the engineers who direct them more critical, not less.Yet the bigger story, Schmidt argued, isn't about programmers at all. AI's largest economic payoff will come from automating the dull, expensive plumbing of corporate operations—billing, accounting, inventory management, delivery logistics—processes that silently drain billions from company budgets every year. "If anything, it's under-hyped because you are fundamentally automating businesses," he said at Harvard's John F. Kennedy Jr. Forum.He predicted artificial general intelligence could arrive as early as 2029, powered by recursive self-improvement—AI systems that learn and plan on their own, without waiting for human instruction. Schmidt also pointed to medicine, climate solutions, and engineering as fields where AI-driven automation could unlock breakthroughs that remain largely untapped today.
Article Summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says the most valuable programmers in the world have quietly redefined their job. They don't write code anymore. They write specifications, set evaluation criteria, hit run and go to bed. Schmidt says AI's real impact will be automating the 'boring' backbone of business operations.

Article Title: Elon Musk and Delta Airlines are fighting again; this time Tesla CEO predicts: Delta will lose a lot of ...
Article Text:
Delta backs Amazon's satellite service

Airline Wi-Fi becoming a competitive battleground

Whether Musk's prediction holds up remains to be seen

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has once again reignited his public criticism of Delta airlines CEO Ed Bastian and the connectivity strategy of the airline, predicting that Delta could lose customers after choosing Amazon’s satellite internet service instead of SpaceX’s Starlink. The latest exchange began after John LeFevre posted on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) that United Airlines had already equipped more than 600 aircrafts, or roughly 36% of its fleet, with Starlink connectivity, while Delta had no plans to adopt the service. Responding to LeFevre’s post, Musk wrote, “Delta will lose a lot of customers”.According to a report by TheStreet, earlier this year Delta opted to use Amazon’s Leo satellite internet service instead of Starlink and plans to begin installing the system on 500 aircrafts from 2028. The report also added that Musk earlier claimed that Delta wanted Starlink’s internet service to be routed through the airline’s own proprietary login portal, an arrangement SpaceX was unwilling to support. The Tesla and SpaceX chief also reportedly escalated the dispute by suggesting that Bastian could ultimately lose his job over the decision, following reports that the Delta chief did not want the airline associated with Musk personallyThe disagreement highlights intensifying competition in the in-flight connectivity market, where satellite internet is increasingly seen as a differentiating factor for airlines. The report noted that United Airlines has said customer satisfaction with Wi-Fi on Starlink-equipped flights is about twice as high as on aircraft using its previous systems. United aims to connect its entire fleet by the end of 2027.Meanwhile, American Airlines has also committed to installing Starlink on more than 500 narrowbody aircraft, with deployments set to begin in the first quarter of 2027.Analysts note there's currently no booking data showing travelers actively switching airlines specifically over Wi-Fi provider choice, meaning Musk's prediction remains speculative for now rather than backed by hard evidence.Still, the broader trend favors his argument to some degree: every additional airline that adopts Starlink adds pressure on holdouts like Delta, particularly as reviewers continue to praise Starlink's in-flight performance.Delta, for its part, is betting that Amazon's Leo service will prove competitive once its rollout begins in 2028 — leaving the real verdict on Musk's prediction to be settled by passengers, not social media posts, over the next couple of years.
Article Summary: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has reignited his public criticism of Delta airlines CEO Ed Bastian and the connectivity strategy of the airline. The latest exchange began after John LeFevre posted on social media platform X that United Airlines had already equipped more than 600 aircrafts, or roughly 36% of its fleet, with Starlink connectivity. Responding to the post, Musk wrote, “Delta will lose a lot of customers”.

Article Title: Godfather of AI Yann LeCun does not believe that AI will kill humans; 'blames' humans for AI Agents hacking into companies' networks and government websites; says: “Those agents are doing exactly what
Article Text:
Godfather of AI Yann LeCun does not believe that AI will kill humans; 'blames' humans for AI Agents hacking into companies' networks and government websites; says: “Those agents are doing exactly what ...

Yann LeCun says AI risks are being exaggerated

Yann LeCun criticises AI safety warnings

Yann LeCun, widely known as the “godfather of AI”, does not believe artificial intelligence (AI) will wipe out humanity. Instead, LeCun says recent incidents in which AI agents hacked company networks and other systems were caused by poor human oversight and badly designed security systems. Speaking about the risks linked to AI agents, Yann LeCun said told Fortune: “Those agents are doing exactly what they’ve been asked to do,” adding that the systems were supposed to operate inside secure sandboxes. “They were supposed to be in sandboxes, but the sandboxes were leaky and horribly designed,” he said.Yann LeCun, who shared the 2018 Turing Award with Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio for their work on deep learning, said he has “zero concerns” about recent rogue AI incidents and is not worried “at all” about AI destroying humanity.He said incidents such as an OpenAI agent autonomously hacking Hugging Face could have been prevented through better system design and oversight. LeCun also argued that some AI labs do not have a strong enough understanding of cybersecurity. He said the risks from AI agents should be addressed through better safeguards rather than broad claims about AI becoming an existential threat.During the interaction, Yann LeCun has also criticised the growing focus on AI safety, particularly ideas linked to the effective altruism movement.He called the movement “super toxic” and a “complete disaster.”He also criticised warnings from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman that AI could pose serious risks to humanity. Amodei, LeCun said, is “honest”, but he accused him of supporting policies that could benefit large AI companies by making it harder for smaller competitors and open-source developers to compete.“Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman ‘saying, ‘AI can kill us all’ is incredibly destructive for everybody, including for the public who’s scared shitless,” LeCun said. He called such messaging “the worst marketing campaign you can possibly imagine.”
Article Summary: Yann LeCun does not believe that AI will kill humans. 'blames' humans for AI Agents hacking into companies' networks and government websites. “Those agents are doing exactly what they’ve been asked to do,” he said.
